StringWithMarkup.String: Ammonium bicarbonate is manufactured by passing carbon dioxide gas countercurrently through a descending stream of aqua ammonia. The reaction is normally carried out in a packed tower or absorption column. Because the reaction is exothermic, cooling the lower portion of the tower is advisable. Concentration of the solution is monitored by determining specific gravity. When the solution is sufficiently saturated, crystallization of ammonium bicarbonate occurs. The crystals are separated from the mother liquor by filtration or centrifugation and washing, and are dried using 50 °C air.

StringWithMarkup.String: /AQUATIC SPECIES/ The effects of /ammonium bicarbonate/ on the early stages of development of Atlantic salmon were studied. The first set of studies, at 13 °C, lasted 53 days and was carried out within the range 0.001 to >6.6 mg NH3/L beginning with the "formed embryo" stage. Accelerated hatching was observed with increasing ammonium carbonate concentrations, but concentrations >0.16 mg NH3/L were lethal for emerging larvae within 12-36 hours. Growth inhibition was observed at 0.07 mg NH3/L. Tissue changes were observed in eyes, brain, fins, and blood of embryos and larvae exposed to concentrations ranging from 0.16 to 6.6 mg NH3/L with more marked changes at higher ammonia concentrations. Reaction to light and mechanical stimulation gradually disappeared with increased ammonia concentration, and the heart rate slowed. Morphological differences in development between experimental and control larvae were observed since 10th day of exposure. At concentrations up to 0.07 mg NH3/L, no significant morphological differences were observed.
